methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $1.0B total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
JetZero is a Series B-stage transportation company founded by Tom O'Leary and Mark Page that has raised over $1.0B to date. The Transportation sector peer universe consists of seven private companies including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Arc Boats, and Parallel Systems, with no public comparables available for direct benchmarking.

The valuation analysis applies one applicable triangulation method due to data constraints. Stage-Progression analysis uses the $1.0B total raised as a proxy baseline and applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B-to-next-stage advancement, yielding an implied valuation of $1.9B. Peer-Median analysis was not applicable because the narrow peer set in Transportation lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables meeting minimum density thresholds (zero same-stage, zero adjacent-stage, zero similar-tier matches identified). A sector-wide median would introduce excessive noise given the heterogeneity of transportation subsectors and business models represented.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $1.6B to $2.2B, centered on $1.9B. This range reflects a ±15% confidence band around the stage-progression median. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the 1.9x multiplier to JetZero's specific risk profile and the absence of narrow peer validation. The single-method triangulation limits conviction and suggests that additional primary diligence on operational metrics and capital efficiency would materially strengthen the valuation thesis.
